title: Minimum Window Substring
statement:
You are given two strings `s` and `t` made of English letters (uppercase and lowercase are different characters). Find the shortest contiguous substring of `s` (a **window**) that contains every character of `t`, counting multiplicity: if `t` contains a letter `k` times, the window must contain that letter at least `k` times. The window may contain other characters as well.

If several windows have the same shortest length, print the one that starts earliest in `s`. If no window of `s` contains all characters of `t`, print `-1`.

**Follow-up:** interviewers (Airbnb, Flipkart) expect working code within about 45 minutes and push to avoid redundant work: no repeated scans of the window and no redundant function calls. Aim for a single left-to-right pass where each character enters and leaves the window at most once.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the string `s`.
The second line contains the string `t`.
outputFormat: Print the shortest window as a string, or `-1` if there is none.
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The window `aybzc` (length 5) contains a, b and c, but `cab` at the end has length 3 and is shorter. No window of length 2 can hold three different letters.
`t` needs two a's and one b. The window `baa` (indices 1 to 3) has length 3, and no shorter window has two a's together with a b.
`s` has only one `a`, but `t` needs two, so no window works.

hints: Count how many copies of each letter `t` needs. A window is valid when every needed count is met. Checking this naively for every window is far too slow.
Use two pointers. Move the right end forward, adding characters, until the window is valid. Then move the left end forward as long as the window stays valid, recording the best length.
Track a single number, how many required characters are still missing, so that you can test validity in O(1) each time a character enters or leaves.
